title: 01 — The Footsteps That Arrive First
html:
The Footsteps That Arrive First

The sounds of your pursuers have finally disappeared. The darkness returns to its familiar silence. Then you hear footsteps. Four sets, moving in perfect unison. You stop. The footsteps ahead stop too. A moment passes. Then one additional footstep echoes in the darkness. Something has taken another step after you stopped moving.

Truth: A manifestation of anticipation/dread makes the party hear their own expected futures. The sounds predict what they fear, not what must happen. The existing wisp guides them toward the noise, retaining its own identity.

Challenge: 3 Chase Points

PF2e Chase-style obstacle. Occultism DC 31, Perception DC 31, Performance DC 31, Survival DC 33. Critical success +2; success +1; failure 0; critical failure -1 (min 0). A genuinely unexpected action based on trust earns 1 free point. Use Kiragon — Footsteps Chase macro.

Failure: If not resolved in three rounds, they escape but must make DC 31 Will saves: failure frightened 1, crit failure frightened 2. No direct Will loss here beyond the running clock.

“Please don't come looking for me.”

The voice is the party's fear of failure, not necessarily Leif.

title: 02 — The Thing That Begs to Be Killed
html:
The Thing That Begs to Be Killed

At first you hear only crying. Then the wisp moves closer, revealing a figure crouched on the ground. Its face changes as if several people are trying to occupy the same body. It looks up. “Please. Please kill me. I can't bear feeling this anymore.”

Truth: Grief is a fragment of Leif. It believes death is release. Yet emotions cannot die here; violence merely disperses it, and it returns. Leaving it behind means it follows the party, quietly sobbing.

Nonviolent victory — 3 Comfort VP

Each PC may use an appropriate skill to comfort (Diplomacy, Medicine, Religion, Occultism DC 31). Crit success +2; success +1; failure 0; crit failure -1 (minimum 0). At 3 VP, Grief consents to follow as part of Leif. Use Kiragon — Grief Comfort macro.

Insight: Grief also proves something or someone mattered. It need not be erased.

GM: No attack can kill it. Optional reward: emotional anchor, which can be spent once to prevent one periodic Erosion Will loss from the Kiragon bell (manual intervention at GM discretion).

title: 03 — The Emotions That Hate Each Other
html:
Joy vs Anger — The Contest of Feelings

“THEY'LL UNDERSTAND!” Anger bellows, pointing at the adventurers. Joy claps excitedly. “Oh! Oh, that's wonderful! Let's make it a game!” “A GAME?! EVERYTHING IS A GAME TO YOU!” “Exactly! And I'm going to win!”

Five-round competition

Every PC begins at 0 Happiness / 0 Anger. The first to reach 5 of either (not both) loses exactly 1 Erosion Will and permanently gains Gift of Joy or Gift of Anger. If neither reaches 5 by the end of five rounds or reconciliation, no reward and no extra loss.

Joy: Everything Is Wonderful [two actions], target within 30 ft Will DC 31; F +1 Happiness; CF +2. Infectious Laughter [one action], ranged +26; hit +1/critical +2 Happiness.

Anger: Everything Is Unfair [two actions], same DC 31 and Anger points. Infuriating Accusation [one action], ranged +26; hit +1/critical +2 Anger.

GM macro: Kiragon — Joy & Anger Contest. Adds and subtracts counters, shows round and wins, automatically calls existing Kiragon api.adjust(actor,'abyssal-erosion','identity',-1,...) when one counter reaches 5, and gives the permanent feat. No other extra Erosion from their attacks.

Nonviolent alternative

Reconcile both: each needs 3 VP with two-action DC 31 Diplomacy, Occultism, or Performance checks. Crit success 2, success 1, failure 0, crit failure -1. Joy learns Anger protects what matters; Anger learns Joy is not denial. Both at 3 stops the contest with no extra penalty for undecided PCs.

Immortality: At 0 HP either disperses one round then reforms. They are not demons and cannot be killed.

title: 04 — The Four Who Are One
html:
The Four Who Are One

Four identical figures stand before you. Their faces are the same, their clothing is the same, and even their voices are indistinguishable. “You came for me. But which of us are you here to save?”

Four versions of Leif: Fear, Shame, Love, Anger. None is fake. Each offers to spare Leif its own pain by being left behind.

Win condition

Acknowledge all four as parts of Leif. The party can use true personal understanding without a roll; otherwise DC 31 Occultism, Religion or Diplomacy; DC 33 Perception for their shared consciousness. The macro Kiragon — Four Who Are One tracks which fragments have been accepted.

Fear: Keeps him alive and cautious. Shame: Holds remorse and reflection. Love: Makes connection possible. Anger: Can protect boundaries and dignity.

When all four are welcomed, they briefly merge into Leif's form: “You found the parts of me. But you haven't found the part that makes them mine.” A heartbeat begins in the darkness. Proceed to Resignation and Leif's Hope.

No one can kill a fragment here; violence is not a solution.

title: 05 — The End of Wanting — Leif’s Hope
html:
Final Boss: The End of Wanting

The wisp guides you until the darkness seems to have an end. An enormous figure crouches before you, dozens of hands curled around something small. Between its fingers, a pale figure resembling Leif. “No. He has hoped enough. I will not let you make him suffer again.”

Important: The guiding wisp has its own established identity. Leif's Hope is the pale humanoid protected by Resignation; it is not the wisp.

Boss: Unique level 16, AC 38, HP 295, Fort +28, Ref +25, Will +30, DC 35 for Nothing Will Change. Creature traits spirit, emotion (NOT demon). Suppresses rather than dies at 0 HP; returns after one round. The party needs 6 Hope VP.

Six Hope Points across three barriers

Per PC, two actions for a rescue check. Critical success +2, success +1, failure 0, critical failure -1 in the current 2-point barrier only. Earn 2 VP per stage. Stage 1: Fear of Failure — Can they accept not being able to promise success? Diplomacy or Occultism DC 31. Stage 2: Fear of Pain — Can they acknowledge care is still worthwhile despite suffering? Diplomacy/Religion DC 31, Medicine DC 33. Stage 3: Fear of Trying Again — Speak directly to Hope with memories of Leif, DC 31 Diplomacy or DC 33 Performance; moving genuine roleplay can score without dice.

Special: Comforting Grief or reconciling Joy/Anger grants one automatic successful point in Stage 2 (at GM choice).

Fractured Certainty: 60+ damage to Resignation in a round suppresses reactions and grants +2 circumstance to next rescue check. Boss can strike to cause frightened; its burst can cause slowed and potentially at most one extra Kiragon Will per PC per round (GM adjudicates).

Resignation: “But what if he fails again?” Hope: “Then I'll be disappointed.” “And what if it hurts?” “Then it will hurt.” “And what if nothing gets better?” “I don't know. But I want to find out.”

At 6 VP, Hope stands up and returns to Leif willingly. Resignation remains; it no longer decides Leif's future. The emotion is not destroyed.

GM macro: Kiragon — Leif’s Hope Boss.
